reasons: Rule fit is defensible: although Section 3.1 is a pure revenue share with no minimum spend, the Section 4.2(a) volume-based Termination Payment (trailing 12-month Net Sales less $800,000, halved) functions as a take-or-pay style exit penalty measured by volume, which the rule's 'no take-or-pay without an exit' position addresses; the finding correctly states there is no minimum purchase commitment and flags only the exit charge.

Redline is directionally correct and pro-Customer: it narrows, rather than expands, our payment obligation by carving out termination for HDI's material breach and termination under Section 1.6, preserving the negotiated economics for a convenience exit consistent with the fallback rather than deleting the clause outright.

Edit is minimal and grammatically clean — a single inserted 'other than (i) ... or (ii) ...' qualifier before the payment obligation; the 0.500 changed-character ratio reflects the length of the inserted carve-out, not an unnecessary rewrite, and no defined terms are disturbed.
Comment is accurate, concise, in first person plural, correctly prefixed, states what changed and why, and cites the playbook position without lecturing.

Caveat (not disqualifying): the asserted content of Section 1.6 (termination 'without penalty') is not among the supplied paragraphs or definitions, so the cross-reference in both the redline and the comment should be confirmed against the executed text before sending; if Section 1.6 does not in fact provide a penalty-free termination right, limb (ii) should be dropped or re-pointed.
